content: Diflorasone is a topical medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, dryness, crusting, scaling, inflammation (swelling), and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It belongs to a class of drugs known as topical steroids, which function by reducing inflammation and itching. Diflorasone is available in the form of a cream or ointment and is applied directly to the skin. Typically, it is used one to three times daily on the affected area. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to apply the medication at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed, and do not apply more or less than prescribed or use it more frequently than instructed. Before applying the medication, thoroughly wash or soak the affected area unless doing so irritates your skin. Apply a thin layer of the cream or ointment sparingly and gently rub it into the skin. If you are using Diflorasone on your face, avoid contact with your eyes. If applying it to a child’s diaper area, do not use tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as this may increase the risk of side effects. Avoid applying cosmetics or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not wrap or bandage the treated area unless specifically instructed by your doctor. If your doctor advises wrapping or bandaging the treated area, follow these steps: Wash or soak the area thoroughly. While the skin is still moist, gently rub the medication into the affected area. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap or Handi-Wrap). For hands, plastic gloves may be used; for feet, plastic bags; and for the scalp, a shower cap. Secure the edges of the plastic wrap to ensure it adheres closely to the skin. If the area is moist, leave the edges partially unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. Leave the plastic wrap in place for the duration specified by your doctor, typically no more than 12 hours per day. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrap is applied. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using Diflorasone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to Diflorasone or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while using this medication. If you forget to apply a dose, do so as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Diflorasone may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: Skin burning, itching, or irritation Dry skin Rash Increased hair growth Skin discoloration Prolonged use of Diflorasone may slow growth in children. Discuss the risks of long-term use with your doctor. If you experience any unusual problems while using this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as they may order tests to monitor your body’s response to Diflorasone. Do not share this medication with others, and do not use it for a skin condition other than the one for which it was prescribed. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
